claim: Biological synaptic transmission is unreliable.

claim: Unreliability of synaptic transmission likely degrades neural circuit performance.

claim: Biophysical mechanisms can increase synaptic reliability.

claim: Energetic costs for reliability were embedded in artificial neural networks with trainable stochastic synapses.

claim: Synapses with lower variability tended to have higher input firing rates.

claim: Evolution may have chanced upon a scheme for implementing Bayesian inference by optimising energy efficiency.

evidence: This is presented as one of two possible interpretations of the findings.

claim: Energy-efficient synapses may display signatures of Bayesian inference without actually using Bayes to reason about uncertainty.
